tool_spec.name: utterance_text_concordance_search
tool_spec.purpose: Searches individual LocoMo utterance_text units rather than session summaries, and augments each hit with same-session context, co-occurrence expansion, morphological matching, fixed speaker-identity scoring, speaker/session/date metadata, relative-time phrases, and name-collision flags so downstream synthesis can quote exact facts, aggregate lists, and disambiguate speakers.
tool_spec.inputs: question: str, corpus: list of documents with pages containing utterance units, top_k: int (clamped 1-25).
tool_spec.outputs: dict with a bounded results list. Each result includes doc_id, node_id, unit_index, page_number, title, score, text, context_text, neighbor_count, source_name, speaker, session_index, date_time, section_name, is_summary, relative_phrases, and reasons. Metadata includes query, counts, applied speaker/session/date filters, expansion_terms, collaborative_cue, relaxed_filters, and name_collisions.
tool_spec.algorithm: 1. Flatten all page units into utterance records with speaker, session, date, and section metadata. 2. Infer optional speaker, session, and date filters from the question text and apply strict filters; if the strict combination is empty, relax filters one at a time. 3. Compute IDF-weighted lexical overlap scores over utterance text and section names, using both surface tokens and lightweight stems, and add a fixed named-speaker bonus when a query token matches the utterance speaker, rather than letting corpus-frequency variation suppress a speaker. Additional bonuses cover quoted phrases, whole-question matches, short exact utterances, and life-stage qualifiers. 4. Use positive lexical hits as pseudo-relevance seeds, derive high-IDF co-occurring expansion terms shared by at least two seeds, and re-score candidates with the expansion. 5. Add a bounded same-session context bonus from neighboring utterance units and attach context_text. 6. Stratify selection across named speakers; for collaborative multi-speaker questions, round-robin over named speakers in question order starting from the last-named speaker so every participant's evidence is represented. 7. Return top_k results sorted by final score with collaborative selection order preserved as a tie-breaker.
tool_spec.complexity: O(N*Q + N*C + N log N) time and O(N) memory, where N is the number of utterance texts, Q is the number of non-stop query tokens, and C is the capped expansion-term count. Session grouping and context extraction are linear in N.
failure_modes: Answer terms with no lexical, morphological, or co-occurrence signal remain unreachable.
Aggressive expansion can add noise when seed utterances are heterogeneous; expansion is capped at 12 shared IDF-weighted terms to limit drift.
Same-session context can boost a tangential neighbor; the context bonus is additive and bounded.
Lightweight suffix matching can occasionally conflate word forms, but its impact is bounded and only used to broaden candidate matching.
Relative-date arithmetic and pronoun/anaphora resolution remain downstream synthesis tasks.
Very high top_k can produce redundant utterances; per-session caps mitigate this.

usage_policy.when_to_call: Call this tool for direct fact lookup before concluding a fact is absent, for list and shared-attribute questions where evidence may live across sessions, and whenever summary-level search returns only generic topic text. Also call it when a question names multiple speakers or asks for a comparison/intersection.
usage_policy.how_to_use_output: Quote the text or context_text fields as verbatim evidence; verify speaker, session_index, and date_time before attributing a fact; aggregate across top-k results when enumerating lists; use relative_phrases together with date_time for relative-date reasoning; consult name_collisions before assigning facts to a person.
usage_policy.fallback: If no positive-score result is returned, drop date/session/speaker filters one at a time and retry with a paraphrased query. If still empty, use session summaries or timeline evidence as a secondary source. Do not declare a fact absent after a single failed summary-level search.
usage_policy.stopping_rule: Stop after at most two query reformulations or when top_k contains positive scored evidence. Only declare absence when relaxed searches still return no relevant snippet.

repair_analysis.what_worked: The repaired primitive still recovers exact utterance-level facts, quoted titles, speaker disambiguation, date anchors, and life-stage qualifiers. It now separates speaker-identity scoring from content-term IDF, so a speaker who appears in many utterances is not penalized, and it preserves collaborative round-robin selection order as a tie-breaker instead of letting a post-selection sort undo the interleaving.
failure_mechanisms: Speaker-name tokens were scored through corpus-wide IDF, so if one participant appeared in multiple utterances their speaker token had lower IDF than a co-participant's name. That made the repeated speaker's evidence lose a near-tie even when round-robin selection had chosen it first.
The previous final sort by score alone discarded collaborative selection order, so a small IDF difference could move the wrong speaker's utterance to the top of a two-speaker shared-activity result.
Morphological matching and same-session context were helpful but could not compensate for speaker-frequency scoring and post-selection reordering.
repair_analysis.scope_boundary: This remains a retrieval primitive, not a reasoning engine. It still cannot resolve pronoun/reference ambiguity, enumerate answer terms with zero lexical or co-occurrence signal, or perform date arithmetic. Those remain synthesis tasks, though the tool supplies same-session context, date anchors, relative-time phrases, morphological matching, fixed speaker-identity scoring, and collaborative multi-speaker selection to support them.

changes: Removed speaker tokens from the IDF map and from the content haystack used for lexical IDF scoring, so corpus frequency of a person's name no longer suppresses evidence by that speaker.

Added a fixed named-speaker bonus: when a query content token is part of the utterance's speaker label, the utterance receives a constant speaker-match score instead of a frequency-dependent IDF score.
Preserved light morphological matching so verb forms such as volunteer/volunteering and run/running are treated as the same lexical family.
Changed selection bookkeeping so collaborative round-robin order is stored and used as a tie-breaker in the final score sort; the highest-scoring result still wins decisive score differences.
Kept pseudo-relevance expansion, same-session context, speaker/session/date filters, life-stage qualifiers, relative-phrase annotations, and name-collision metadata.
Kept conservative fallback: if the strict speaker/session/date combination is empty, filters are relaxed one at a time and metadata records relaxed_filters.

prediction.expected_quality_effect: Should retain the exact-fact and metadata wins from the earlier version while fixing the remaining shared-activity case. Morphological matching still lets the gold-bearing utterance enter the candidate set, fixed speaker-identity scoring prevents frequency artifacts, and preserved round-robin tie-order lets the needed participant's evidence reach the top instead of being unseated by a small score artifact.
prediction.expected_cost_effect: Output size remains bounded because context_text is capped at 1000 characters per result and top_k is capped at 25. Input token use and latency remain similar since the corpus scan is unchanged; the stem map, fixed speaker bonus, and order-aware selection all run in linear time.
prediction.falsification_test: Hold out 10 shared-attribute or same-session questions where the gold answer depends on two named speakers or on a fact co-occurring in one session. Fail the repair if the gold-bearing utterance is absent from top_k in more than 2 cases, or if expansion/context introduces a wrong supporting answer in more than 2 cases.

novelty_claim: A focused repair to the same utterance-concordance capability: it separates speaker-identity scoring from corpus-frequency IDF, adds a fixed named-speaker match bonus, and preserves collaborative round-robin tie-order. It does not add a second tool, does not memorize benchmark cases, and remains a general retrieval primitive over existing LocoMo utterance_text fields.
